name: Qatar Investment Authority

summary.text: The Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) is the sovereign wealth fund of the State of Qatar, established in 2005 by Amiri Decision No. 22 of 2005 and reorganized by Amiri Decision No. 34 of 2023; it reports to the Supreme Council for Economic Affairs and Investment. Its real-estate arm Qatari Diar, established in 2005, signed an agreement with Dar Global on April 30, 2025 to develop a Trump International Golf Club and Trump-branded villas within the Simaisma master plan north of Doha. The QIA is a limited partner in Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners: a September 2024 Senate Finance Committee letter identified Qatari sovereign funds among investors paying 2 percent fees on about $1 billion of commitments, and Bloomberg reported in December 2024 that QIA and Abu Dhabi's Lunate had committed a further $1.5 billion. In August 2023 the QIA bought the Park Lane Hotel in Manhattan from a group led by Steve Witkoff for about $623 million.

facts.claim: The QIA describes itself as established in 2005 to protect and grow Qatar's financial assets and diversify the economy. Its charter was Amiri Decision No. 22 of 2005; on May 16, 2023 the Amir issued Amiri Decision No. 34 of 2023 reorganizing the QIA and replacing the 2005 decision. The QIA reports to the Supreme Council for Economic Affairs and Investment, and its mission is 'developing, investing and managing the State reserve funds and other assets assigned to it by SCEAI'.

facts.claim: Qatari Diar is a real-estate company established in 2005 by the Qatar Investment Authority; it manages the QIA's real-estate portfolio and acts as master developer on projects. On April 30, 2025 Qatari Diar and Dar Global signed an agreement at Qatari Diar's headquarters in Lusail to develop Trump International Golf Club and Trump-branded villas within the Simaisma master plan, about 40 kilometres north of Doha.

facts.claim: In a September 24, 2024 letter to Affinity Partners, Senate Finance Committee chairman Ron Wyden wrote that the firm had committed capital from foreign clients of approximately $3 billion, that Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund paid a 1.25 percent fee on $2 billion, and that five other foreign investors, including sovereign wealth funds from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates and Taiwanese billionaire Terry Gou, paid 2 percent on the remaining $1 billion. The letter is a committee inquiry, not a finding; it does not state the QIA's individual amount.
facts.quote: five other foreign investors, including sovereign wealth funds from Qatar, the United Arab Emirates ("UAE"), and Taiwanese billionaire Terry Gou, are paying even higher rates of 2 percent on the remaining $1 billion

facts.claim: Bloomberg reported on December 20, 2024 that Affinity Partners had raised an additional $1.5 billion from the Qatar Investment Authority and Abu Dhabi's Lunate and extended its debut fund's investment period to 2029. The reports give a combined figure and not the QIA's share. Jared Kushner said the talks began in February 2024 and closed before the U.S. election, and named PIF, Lunate and QIA as his three largest limited partners.

facts.claim: On March 19, 2026 Senator Ron Wyden and Representative Robert Garcia wrote to Affinity Partners requesting, among other things, the amounts invested in and contributed to its funds by each investor in each calendar year from 2021 to 2025. No published response was found.
facts.quote: the amount invested in, and any amounts contributed to, private investment funds managed by Affinity in each calendar year from 2021 to 2025

facts.claim: In August 2023 the QIA bought the 46-story Park Lane Hotel at 36 Central Park South in Manhattan from a group led by Steve Witkoff for about $623 million, according to property records; the sale was first reported by PincusCo. The QIA was later reported to be planning a redevelopment of the property as a hotel with condominiums and residences.
facts.quote: The Qatar Investment Authority paid nearly $623 million to acquire the 46-story hotel at 36 Central Park South from Steve Witkoff's company, property records show.

openQuestions: The QIA does not publish its assets under management; third-party estimates for 2025-26 range from about $510 billion to $600 billion, and none came from a primary source reached in this session, so no size figure is recorded.

The QIA's individual commitment to Affinity Partners (as opposed to the combined $1.5 billion with Lunate and the combined $1 billion in the Wyden letter) was not found in any source; the March 2026 Wyden-Garcia letter requests year-by-year figures.

The Simaisma licence-fee figure of $5.25 million comes from The National's reading of the 2026 OGE disclosure; the filing itself was not opened and other outlets group Gulf licensing income differently.
Qatari Diar's founding year is given as 2005 by Qatari Diar and MEED and as 2004 by another trade source; the entity's own date is used.
